moonwell_blighted_roots.description: The roots beneath the Moonwell have begun to come up black at the edges, like frost creeping across glass. Pennarin has traced it to the Twilight Rootbinders, who sing to the roots in the dark under the grove. Five samples of what they carry will tell her how far the rot has gone, and how long the Grove has left.
moonwell_blighted_roots.accept_text: The Rootbinders sing to the roots, and the roots sing back, and the song is wrong. I heard it from the top of the stairs and I have not slept properly since. Bring me what they carry. Use a cloth, and please don't tell me whether it was warm.
moonwell_blighted_roots.turn_in_text: Black at the core, and warm. That is not sap. Thank you, I needed to know, even though I did not want to. Say nothing of it in the market. Fear spreads faster than any rot, and we have enough of that already.

moonwell_gloomcap_sacs.description: Below the Moonwell the gloomcap sporelings are spreading, and the healers cannot agree whether the growth can be burned out or must be cut out. The answer sits in the spore sacs they carry. Shalasyr wants six, unbroken, studied before the fungus finds the roots of the Grove itself.
moonwell_gloomcap_sacs.accept_text: Gently. They burst, and then you'll smell it for a week, and so will everyone you walk past. Six, unbroken. The healers asked me to find someone expendable for this. I told them I didn't know anyone like that. Then I met you, and I stopped being so sure.
moonwell_gloomcap_sacs.turn_in_text: Unbroken. I'm impressed, and a little disgusted. The healers will want to know what these are feeding on, and I intend to let them find out slowly. Go and wash before you see Pennarin. She has a very good nose and no patience for the Hollow.

moonwell_hollow_cull.description: The Hollow beneath the Moonwell was never a place to walk alone, and what lives there now is not what the Sentinels remember. The Rotlashers grow bolder, the Corrupted Moon Guard still wear their old armor, and the Rootbinders keep singing. Pennarin needs the Hollow thinned so a party can reach the grove at the bottom.
moonwell_hollow_cull.accept_text: Go down in company. The Hollow was never meant to be walked alone, and it is not what it was. The Moon Guard down there were mine once, and they will know your faces before you know theirs. Take a healer. Take someone to hold the line. And if you see a face you recognise, remember it isn't them any more.
moonwell_hollow_cull.turn_in_text: You came back. That's more than the last party managed, and they were braver than they were wise. I'll be telling the families, so forgive me if I look at you a moment too long. It's how I remember who did right by us.

moonwell_mosshide.description: At the heart of the Hollow's spread sits a gloomcap the size of a house, so old the Sentinels gave it a name: Mosshide. Everything in the Hollow grows toward it, and the rot feeds on it like a hearth. If it falls, the spread loses its anchor. Nobody has ever felled it.
moonwell_mosshide.accept_text: Mosshide was here before the Moonwell's lamps. Before the Sentinels, if the old songs are right. It won't go quietly, and the spores will do half its fighting for it. Keep your party tight, and save your breath for the end, not the beginning.
moonwell_mosshide.turn_in_text: Then the spread has a hole in it. Good. Rest while you can. Maelwyn is next, and she will be harder. I won't pretend I'm glad to send you after her. But I'd rather it were someone with steady hands.

moonwell_maelwyn.description: Maelwyn Blightbloom tended the Moonwell for a hundred years, and Pennarin called her friend for most of them. Now she is the Blight's flower, rooted where the water used to run clear. The Moonwell cannot be healed while she stands there. Pennarin asks it of you because she cannot do it herself.
moonwell_maelwyn.accept_text: She still has the face I remember. Don't let that slow your hand. If she speaks, you may answer, and I won't ask what was said. But when it's time, do it cleanly. She taught me how to hold a lamp. I don't want her to be afraid.
moonwell_maelwyn.turn_in_text: ...Thank you. I'll tell the others the water is clear. I won't tell them how it looked. I think I'd like to sit by the Moonwell tonight, if the Hollow lets it be quiet, and remember her with the lamp.

barrows_hunters_horns.description: The huntsmen buried in the Howling Barrows still carry their horns, and the horns still sound whenever the wind touches them. Grunt Bloodfang has had three nights of it at the post and nobody has slept well. Five shards of the horn-bone brought out would quiet the hill, and a good horn might even ring true as a Horde signal.
barrows_hunters_horns.accept_text: I don't care whose horns they are. I want them quiet. Three nights, I've listened to a dead man blow for his hounds, and my recruits are starting to answer. Bring me five shards. If the bone cuts a decent signal horn, even better.
barrows_hunters_horns.turn_in_text: Hm. Still howls when the wind touches it. Gives me the chills. Good work. I'll have a signal horn cut from it. If it ever calls anything, I'd rather it was our people and not theirs.

barrows_rimebone_cull.description: The Hunt-King's road runs through the Barrows, and it is kept by frozen things: Rimebone Hounds, Barrow Wights, and Howling Wraiths who never stopped running. As long as they walk, the place keeps singing the Hunt's old song, and the song is getting louder each night. Vashj wants the road silent.
barrows_rimebone_cull.accept_text: Dead things in a cold hole. It's not complicated. Go in with friends, come out with the job done. Don't stand still in the cold. The wights feed on anyone who stops. I'll know if you've been thorough.
barrows_rimebone_cull.turn_in_text: The howling is thinner. Not gone, but thinner. That's your next job. You look half frozen. There's a pot on at the post. It's not good, but it's hot, and in the Barrows you'll want to remember what hot feels like.

barrows_wintermaw.description: In the Houndkeepers' Crypt a hound the size of a warhorse lies chained to the floor. The chains are old, and the grudge is older, and the howl has been bleeding through the whole Barrows for as long as anyone in the post can remember. Vashj wants it ended by someone willing to fight a grievance as well as a beast.
barrows_wintermaw.accept_text: It won't come to you. You'll go to it. Take a healer and a good reason. It doesn't want your life specifically. It wants anyone's. If you have somewhere to be afterwards, hold it in your head. That helps.
barrows_wintermaw.turn_in_text: The howl has stopped. I didn't know how much of the wind it was until it did. I stood on the wall an hour, listening to nothing. I'll not say I missed it. But I understood it, and I didn't enjoy that.

barrows_hunt_king.description: At the far end of the Barrows lies Hunt-King Valorin, still hunting in his sleep. The hounds and wights were only his pack. War Mage Grimtotem will not have a dead king's hunt ranging across Horde land, and he does not want to learn where Valorin thinks the border is.
barrows_hunt_king.accept_text: The Wild Hunt never ended. It just went underground. Let's make sure it stays there. If he speaks, it'll be in an old tongue, and you'll understand it anyway, which is half of what makes him dangerous. He doesn't need to be heard to be obeyed.
barrows_hunt_king.turn_in_text: He rode out of the world a long time ago. Now he's finally ridden all the way home. I don't know if he'd have thanked you. I do.

groms_garrison_cull.description: Grom's Rest has become a demon barracks. Satyrs, imps and fel-touched hounds crowd the hall beyond the gate, and the outpost's scouts report more arriving every night. Grimtotem wants the garrison thinned so a real party can push through to whatever sits behind it.
groms_garrison_cull.accept_text: This is a dungeon, not a stroll. Bring a full party and your potions, and then bring me proof the hall is clearer. I've sent enough people down there who thought they were stronger than they were. I'd rather send people who know exactly how strong they are.
groms_garrison_cull.turn_in_text: Good. The gate is no longer a wall of bodies. Now find out what they were guarding. I have a feeling it isn't the throne. I have a feeling it's something worse, and they were only the door.

groms_legion_brands.description: The Felguard Legionnaires of Grom's Rest wear fel-iron plate stamped with the Legion's mark. Vashj has heard that the Legion's gold reaches Ashenvale by some other road, and the brands could tell her which. Five plates, taken from the dead, would be enough to trace a foundry back to the hand that paid for it.
groms_legion_brands.accept_text: Take them off the dead, not the living. The living will object. And don't read the stamps aloud. I don't want to know who's been paid until I know whom to ask about it. Five plates will do.
groms_legion_brands.turn_in_text: These are stamped in a Legion foundry I know. Someone is shipping weapons through Ashenvale, and I know who to ask. Thank you. Please don't tell the others yet. People who learn this sort of thing early make bad choices, and I'd like at least one clear head in this post.

groms_satyr_warlord.description: The Satyr Warlord rules the western hall of Grom's Rest. He is a detour rather than a duty, and nobody would blame a party for skipping him. But Vashj knows a warlord left alive recruits, and his head on a spear carries a message further than any dispatch.
groms_satyr_warlord.accept_text: Skippable, I know. Do it anyway. A warlord left alive is a warlord who recruits. A head on a spear is the only language satyrs respect. It's tedious, but it's cheaper than a war.
groms_satyr_warlord.turn_in_text: Good. That kind of loud ends in a very particular silence. I've heard it before and never got used to it. A stillness after a warlord falls, like the world taking a breath. You'll learn to listen for it.

groms_void_handmaiden.description: In the eastern gathering of Grom's Rest, a Void Handmaiden binds satyrs to something that was never made to be bound. The ones it touches stop remembering who they were, and do not seem to mind. Grimtotem has spent his life fighting fel and fire. He has no answer for a thing that simply takes you apart.
groms_void_handmaiden.accept_text: Void magic isn't like fel. Fel burns. Void forgets. Take someone who remembers you. A friend, a companion, anyone who'll say your name when you can't. I'm not joking. The first fool to go in alone came back as a stranger.
groms_void_handmaiden.turn_in_text: I feel lighter. I think it is lighter. Thank you. I don't know what she was taking, but I think we were all paying for it somehow.

groms_doomguard.description: The only road to the throne runs north from the hub of Grom's Rest, and a Doomguard Sentinel stands in it. It does not tire, does not sleep, and does not move. It has never left its post in all the years the outpost has watched it, and three more rooms lie behind it before the throne.
groms_doomguard.accept_text: It doesn't tire, it doesn't sleep, it doesn't move. You'll have to persuade it. Forcefully. Bring everything you have and then a little more. It's a long walk back if it goes badly, and I've yet to meet a doomguard that held a grudge about a first attempt.
groms_doomguard.turn_in_text: One down. Three rooms behind it, and the throne beyond. Press on. There'll be a hot meal for whoever comes out. If it's you, you'll want it. If it isn't, I'll eat it myself and think of you fondly.

groms_corrupted_ancient.description: Deeper in, an ancient has been bent into a demon's horror. What was once a grove warden is a thing that rots and sings. The Sentinels will not speak of it, and the druids of the forest cannot bring themselves to look. Grimtotem has no such luxury. It stands between the party and the throne.
groms_corrupted_ancient.accept_text: It was a protector once. Remember that when your hand slows. Then remember it can't be saved. I've seen the Sentinels' faces when they say its name. If it still has one. I wish I had better words. I never found them either.
groms_corrupted_ancient.turn_in_text: I'll tell the druids it fell fighting. That's as close to the truth as they can bear. I think it was fighting the whole time, somewhere underneath. I think that's the only reason it was still a tree and not a pit.

groms_felguard_overseer.description: The Felguard Overseer holds the Bone Hall, the last gate before the Inner Sanctum, and he wears the fingerprints of whoever sent him. If the Legion has a hand in Ashenvale, the proof is on his collar. Vashj wants it brought back, because the Warchief does not move armies on stories.
groms_felguard_overseer.accept_text: Bring me his collar. It will tell us who he answered to. The Legion doesn't forget its own, and it doesn't forgive an overseer who dies unmarked. Take care what you carry back. I don't want to learn what it's worth by watching someone try to take it from you.
groms_felguard_overseer.turn_in_text: A Legion collar, as I thought. Now we know who has been sending the demons. I'll carry this to Orgrimmar myself. You have given the Warchief something that will take him a year to stop thinking about. That's a good day's work.

groms_lord_nightmare.description: At the heart of Grom's Rest sits the eldritch horror the demons have been feeding, a thing that was never meant to see daylight and has been dreaming for a very long time. Kill it, and the throne is empty and the Legion loses its foothold in Ashenvale. Grimtotem has nothing to offer but a warning.
groms_lord_nightmare.accept_text: I have no better advice than this: don't look at it directly. And don't die. I've seen what it leaves in the ones who did, and I'd rather not see it again. Go. Come back.
groms_lord_nightmare.turn_in_text: ...The silence is unbelievable. Rest, hero. You've earned the quiet. A hundred of my soldiers couldn't have done that. I'm glad you're on our side.

bfd_garrison.description: Under the cliffs beyond Zoram Strand, a flooded temple has become a naga garrison. Lookout Taelanor has watched them go in for weeks and has not seen one come out. It is not a raid, only a quiet and steady build-up, and she wants its warriors thinned before it empties onto the Strand.
bfd_garrison.accept_text: I've counted them going in. I haven't counted them coming out. That's the part that frightens me. Go down in company and thin them. If you see something that looks like a door, don't open it. I've dreamed that door more than once, and it's always already open.
bfd_garrison.turn_in_text: Eight. They'll replace them, but not tonight. I wrote the number down. I'm glad it isn't higher. I'll go on watching the water. It's the only thing I know how to do, and it's easier knowing someone is down there between me and it.

bfd_ghamoo_ra.description: A giant turtle the naga revere as a god guards the outer caverns of Blackfathom. It is the size of a boat, and old enough that the worship may not be misplaced. Taelanor wants it ended and its shell broken, because while it blocks the way, the Strand cannot see what lies behind it.
bfd_ghamoo_ra.accept_text: They worship it. I'd find that sweet if it weren't the size of a boat and hungry. Break it, and take the way. It won't give you peace. The old ones never do. But it has fed on the drowned for centuries, and I'd rather the drowned stopped being fed.
bfd_ghamoo_ra.turn_in_text: A god, they said. It died as easily as a turtle. I'll remember that the next time I hear the naga pray. I'll also remember you didn't smile when you told me. Not many don't.

bfd_lady_sarevess.description: Lady Sarevess commands the naga of the Deeps' upper halls, and rules them with a smile and a long memory. If she falls, her warriors will fight each other for her chair, and that is a month of quiet for the Strand. Taelanor has heard her voice in dreams, and wants it silenced.
bfd_lady_sarevess.accept_text: She'll offer you terms. I wouldn't read them. Cut her down and spare me the sound of her voice in my dreams. She's clever, and very good at sounding like she's on your side. She's never been on anyone's side but her own.
bfd_lady_sarevess.turn_in_text: Without her, the halls will fight over her chair for a month. That's a month the Strand sleeps. Thank you. I'll tell Illyen she can finish the boat. I think I might sleep tonight too, for the first time in a long time.

bfd_gelihast.description: Gelihast has gathered the murlocs of the Deeps under a single nasty banner, and wears a crown stitched from a fisherman's net. It is Illyen's net, taken from one of her boats, and she wants it back. She cares very little what happens to the king, but a great deal about the knot.
bfd_gelihast.accept_text: He wears my boat's net as a crown. MY net. Bring it back. It's patched and it stinks and I want it. The rest of the murlocs will scatter. They always do when the loudest one stops being loud. It's the only true thing I know about them.
bfd_gelihast.turn_in_text: That's my knot! Look at that, he left it. The fool. Thank you. I'll sink another boat in his honour. A better one. Don't tell anyone, but I was a little fond of the old stinker. He had taste in nets. Bad taste in everything else.

bfd_hydra_fangs.description: The murloc hydras of Blackfathom shed fangs as they grow, and the fangs hold an edge better than steel. Illyen has wanted a set for her tool-rack for years. Six taken from the hydras would see her through the next dozen hulls.
bfd_hydra_fangs.accept_text: A hydra fang will cut a rope under tension and never go dull. Six, and I'll have a tool rack worth showing off. They hiss when they're cut, I'm told. I'm told a lot of things. Don't tell me which are true.
bfd_hydra_fangs.turn_in_text: Six. And not a chip. These are going straight in the rack. I'll sharpen nothing for a year. I'd offer you a drink, but I only keep tar. If you ever need a boat built, you know where I am.

bfd_tide_callers.description: Two of the Deeps' deeper masters hold the inner temple: Lorgus Jett, who commands the tide, and Old Serra'kis, who commands what the tide has swallowed. They have worked together for longer than the Strand has had a name. Taelanor says nothing smaller than a full party should try it.
bfd_tide_callers.accept_text: Two of them, deeper in. You'll have to go through both, and it isn't a job for fewer than a full party, Lookout or not. If you hear water that isn't there, trust it. I'm never sure whether the sea is on our side, but I know it isn't on theirs.
bfd_tide_callers.turn_in_text: Both. I felt the water settle. I'd have missed it if I'd been watching the sea instead of you. Sit, if you like. I don't say that to many. It means I trust you, and I'd like to hear what you saw.

bfd_kelris.description: Twilight Lord Kelris hides at the temple's heart, putting the Twilight's Hammer's work into the mouths of dying men. He does not need to fight to be dangerous. The longer he talks, the more reasonable he sounds, and the more of the Strand starts to wonder whether he might be right.
bfd_kelris.accept_text: He works in whispers. Don't listen. Cut him down. I know that sounds simple. It isn't. He'll say something true, then something that sounds true, and by the time you notice you'll be agreeing. Keep your friends close, and their names closer.
bfd_kelris.turn_in_text: Silent. I'd forgotten silence could be so loud. One more below him, and it ends. I don't want to hope. I haven't had a reason in a long while, and I find I'm being careless with it. Be careful. Please.

bfd_aku_mai.description: At the bottom of Blackfathom sleeps Aku'mai, a thing the naga call the Devourer. It has slept for as long as the Strand has had fishermen, and if it wakes, the Strand will be the least of the world's worries. Taelanor wants it ended while it dreams, or left entirely alone.
bfd_aku_mai.accept_text: It's the last thing in the Deeps. Kill it while it sleeps, or don't go at all. I'll be on the wall, watching the water. If it rises, I'll light the beacon, and you'll know how it went. If it doesn't, thank you.
bfd_aku_mai.turn_in_text: Then it's over. I'll sleep tonight. You earned that, and the Strand's gratitude. Take the pearl, if it still glows. I don't know what it is, and I'm not sure I want to. But if anyone can carry it without being changed, I'd like it to be someone who has earned it.
